vercel.$skipRegistration_why: Real and working, and 9 vocabulary spells reference a Vercel portal — so it stays in the catalog as declared capability. But it is NOT registered at user scope: the claude.ai Vercel connector already provides these tools as mcp__claude_ai_Vercel__*, and registering this endpoint too would put two Vercel servers in every session. setup.sh honours this flag.

$comment: kun's MCP catalog — the DECLARED fleet, and the input health.sh counts. Claude Code does NOT read this file; setup.sh copies it to ~/.claude/mcp.json (also not read, but health.sh requires it and derives ROLE from it) and separately registers each entry for real via `claude mcp add-json -s user`. Pruned 2026-08-19 from 25 to 17: eight entries were unregistered not by oversight but because they are broken — design-system-analyzer (npm 404 (@yajihum/design-system-mcp)); memory-bank (npm 404 (@memory-bank/mcp-server)); algolia (local binary ~/.claude/bin/algolia-mcp is missing); gcloud (shell wrapper, speaks no JSON-RPC — not an MCP server); keychain (shell wrapper, speaks no JSON-RPC — not an MCP server); vercel (deliberate dedup — the claude.ai Vercel connector already covers it); neon (case-collides with the live user-scope `Neon`; wrong transport besides); postgres (@bytebase/dbhub — wrong driver, redundant with Neon). Every remaining entry documents a server that is live at user scope today. Asymmetry left deliberately unfixed: Neon, browser, browser-headed and higgs are live at user scope but absent here; adding them changes project_mcp again for no gain. The per-server `description` field is kun's own annotation and is stripped (del(.description)) before registration — it is not part of the MCP config schema.
